what_this_proves: Every artifact version now says who asked for it, which Python and library versions rendered it, and what it is made of; an edit becomes the next version of the same artifact under the spec's own rules; a clone is a new artifact that names its source; deletion follows the owner's policy and leaves the record; two versions or artifacts are compared in a sentence that names what differs, with a diff; an image the creative path stored becomes an artifact with its own copy; and none of the lifecycle words fire without an artifact in focus.

found_on_the_way.never_invented_on_version_two: an edit's paragraphs are scanned by the same rule as a create; the edit sentence's numbers are merged into spoken_numbers so the owner's own figure is admitted and the model's is refused (test: 99999 refused, then admitted when spoken).
found_on_the_way.image_copy: registering an image under the artifact's own key was necessary so that delete (which removes render objects) cannot remove the creative run's output.
found_on_the_way.executive_actor_ref: the executive activity has no run id in scope at the artifact step; the actor's ref is the step kind, the run is on the ledger.
found_on_the_way.illegal_state_transition: a clone (new artifact, DRAFT) and an image registration walked DRAFT -> READY, which app.artifacts.state forbids (the voice clone failed as internal_bug); both now walk DRAFT -> CANONICAL_READY -> RENDERS_PENDING -> READY like the factory.
found_on_the_way.formulas_did_not_move: appending a row to the budget sheet left its fixed-cell formulas (A6 'KDV', B6 '=B5*0.2') where they were, so the independent xlsx validation found the totals row overwritten and marked version two invalid; append_row now shifts every formula key and reference at or below the first row under the data.
found_on_the_way.duplicate_section: append_section accepted a heading that already existed, producing two sections of one name that replace/remove could not tell apart; it is now refused by name.
found_on_the_way.edit_refusal_class: apply_edit wrapped the spec's own invented-number refusal as invalid_edit, so the voice receipt said 'does not fit' instead of 'the numbers do not match what you said'; the spec's refusals now keep their class.

(artifact focused -> no tool, because M22 had no delete); B42 req 412 adds that delete, so the case failed on the new route.
